issues.title: Disclosure quietness and reversible disclosure are not covered by the approved route
issues.rationale: BRIEF requires disclosure to toggle all heading/body pairs with no caller callback. In every case the sole disclosure action is action 1, opening it; there is no disclosure event assertion and no independently checkpointed state immediately bound to that activation. The only event checks bind choice action 2, primary action 4 and caller update action 6. A later empty caller-update interval cannot prove that action 1 emitted no callback. No action closes the disclosure in the same model. The closed-content proposition names body paragraphs only, while heading assertions become N/A; it does not explicitly establish that closed chapter headings are absent. API additionally requires disclosure to remain enabled after a request, but no disclosure enabled assertion or post-request disclosure activation covers that requirement.
issues.revision_needed: Independently extend the obligation index and approved action/state/event routes to cover successful disclosure activation with its own exact quiet interval, same-model close behavior, both members of a closed heading/body pair, and disclosure enabled after request. Preserve real original action indices in any newly authored revision. No product defect is asserted.

issues.title: The explicit storage-over-network priority never has a competing network gate
issues.rationale: The status-label obligation claims guard precedence, but P1 and H1 reach insufficient storage only after a replacement whose meteredConnection is false. P2 replacement is metered but has enough storage. Thus none of the sealed states has insufficient storage and meteredConnection && wifiOnly together, so the explicit storage-priority clause has no distinguishing route. This is a semantic gap even though requirement_routes.audit returns an empty must_route_gaps array. The API and frozen rule types can support an independently authored competing-gates fixture and status/enabled assertions; the current source-pinned fixtures do not.
issues.revision_needed: Add an independently fixed scenario/stimulus with the two gates simultaneously active and a source-backed Storage needed expectation on both platforms. Do not silently reinterpret the existing fixtures or declare predicate coverage from JSON rule presence.

issues.title: The all-text wrapping requirement is narrower in the approved propositions
issues.rationale: BRIEF requires all text to wrap without line limits. The two wrapping questions cover the title and expanded body paragraphs only. Exact native label assertions establish complete accessible strings, not complete visible strings. The horizontal-clipping and row-overlap propositions can both be true while a subtitle, status, chapter heading, disclosure label, choice label or primary label truncates within its own bounds. Those other text roles have no independently approved wrapping/no-truncation proposition. This matters especially in the separately fixed narrow/large profile.
issues.revision_needed: Add source-backed atomic wrapping/no-truncation coverage for every required text role, with both independent judges inspecting the original full state sweep. Do not use an AX label or an unavailable computed SwiftUI font as proof of visible wrapping.

issues.title: The explicit minimum status-text inset has no matching verification route
issues.rationale: BRIEF separately says status text starts at least 16 native units inside the painted band and keeps its leading 4% empty. The only status pixel rule samples normalized x=0.012..0.035. Its dominant solid fill can establish that small sampled strip, not a 16 pt/dp text inset. The API deliberately places the status identifier/label on the whole painted band; no separately bound text allocation, gte inset rule, or explicit qualitative question covers this minimum. Internal nominal layout tokens are advisory, but this sentence states a minimum without making it advisory; this review does not silently change its priority. The hidden RTL profile also requires that any leading-edge proposition distinguish logical leading from the pixel policy's physical-left normalized coordinates.
issues.revision_needed: The independent design owner must fix an honest verification route for the 16-unit minimum and its direction semantics. Exact computed SwiftUI padding cannot be fabricated, and the existing 3.5%-edge fill sample cannot be promoted into that measurement.

issues.title: Several explicit component constraints are absent from the obligation ledger
issues.rationale: BRIEF requires caller-supplied whole MB values without measuring disk, recording a request without fetching audio, parent-owned scrolling with no nested scroller, and no fixed-height blank rows inserted to manufacture scrolling. These are stated component responsibilities/prohibitions, but the 44-entry obligation index and routes file do not explicitly include them. Pixel color, vertical flow order, and full-sweep reachability do not establish the absence of I/O, nested scrolling, or artificial spacer rows. The thin bridges comply by static inspection, but that does not prove these future production behaviors. An independently defined, source-bound implementation audit could cover the source-only constraints later; none is in the frozen acceptance contract.
issues.revision_needed: Index these mandatory ownership/side-effect constraints and define an independent feasible verification disposition tied to the actual production source/host. Do not infer them from screenshots or add invented native computed properties.

issues.title: Two narrow reference states draw status text beyond their painted band
issues.rationale: The P2 permitted/requested reference PNG/SVG keeps the status band at x=40..240 with a single status text line. Inspection of the actual supplied PNGs finds exact navy ink to x=253 and x=268 inclusive, respectively, within the status band's y interval. The requested text therefore also extends past the component right edge x=264. reference-inspection.json records 39 and 76 exact navy pixels outside the band. This is a static-reference discrepancy, not a native product defect or a claimed computed font result. The brief already states that reference font rasterization is not an acceptance oracle, so this issue does not by itself make the UI impossible.
issues.revision_needed: Align the independent narrow reference's wrapping illustration with the unchanged all-text wrapping requirement in a new sealed revision; keep its illustrative/native-measurement distinction explicit.

remaining_limits: SDK-free feasibility only: no compiler/build/device/simulator/native screenshot result was obtained. Future native semantic allocation, real control frames, solid color mapping, original callback dispatch and scroll budget must pass the already required preflight/acquisition.

Hash identity and consistent reconstruction cannot independently certify the design author's process or a complete interpretation of prose. Proposal approval.json status is independently_authored_preimplementation_proposal, not final feasibility approval.

The selected matrix is not a Cartesian truth table. Equality storage boundary, reverse Wi-Fi toggle, eligible Wi-Fi-only/true request, nonmetered ready initial state, and reverse disclosure activation are not selected. The explicit competing-gates precedence and disclosure requirements are blockers above, not merely sampling disclaimers.
Same-ID model updates are explicitly unspecified by API.md and are not silently added as a requirement.

Exact computed SwiftUI typography/text color/internal layout allocations remain advisory. The ink mark proves only its own sampled solid role. The unused waiting palette anchor is not runtime-exercised; no alternative status-color mapping was invented.
Canvas/surface pixel strips establish only the original eligible sampled regions; they do not prove all canvas pixels, generic padding, a physical hit area, or text ink.
Two independent qualitative judges remain a future required acceptance stage. Their agreement is a review outcome, not native computed style or external human gold.
Private caller values and RTL inputs are preserved only in the restricted T2 design/review artifacts. This review adds no hidden caller data to production or builder inputs.
